question.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
question.text: This emperor modernized Japan during the 19th century under his namesake "restoration." This man was presented with the Charter Oath, the first constitution of modern Japan.
question.answerHtml: Emperor Meiji [may-ee-jee] (accept Meiji the Great or Mutsuhito ) – Page 4 – Packet 8
question.clue: This man's governing philosophy was outlined in thefive point "Charter Oath" and would lead to the creation of the position of Prime Minister along with a largely powerless parliament.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Edo period.
swap.text: This is the modern-day name of the city of Edo, for which the Edo period was named. It is also the modern-day capital of Japan.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Amity and Commerce was signed on a ship in the bay of this city, and the capital of the Showa period was this city.

question.leadin: Give the following about surprise attacks in Japanese history.
question.text: In the 1560 Battle of Okehazama, this daimyo's forces sneaked to the rear of the opposing army, killing the opposing leader at his tent. This unifier of Japan was succeeded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.
question.clue: This man was forced to commit seppuku after being betrayed by Akechi Mitsuhide at Honno-ji.

swap.leadin: Its founder was one of the three great unifiers of a certain country, along with Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
swap.text: Name this shogunate, which was established after the Battle of Sekigahara and ruled from 1603 to 1868.
swap.clue: In the later part of this period, known as the Bakumatsu, the Convention of Kanagawa was signed, signaling the reversal of this period's sakoku isolationist policy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Meiji Restoration.
question.text: The Meiji Restoration led to the decline of this warrior class of Japan. Members of this warrior nobility of Japan followed a code of ethics called bushido.
question.clue: Their status as their nation's only armed force was ended by Emperor Meiji, and they soon lost their right to wear the katana in public.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about periods of Japanese history.
swap.text: This period began after Tokugawa leyasu won the battle of Sekigahara and saw artistic development and prosperity in Japan for over 200 years.
swap.answerHtml: Edo period [prompt on Tokugawa Shogunate by asking “what period did the Tokugawa Shogunate rule over?”]
swap.clue: Its end is known by a term meaning "closing of the curtain."

question.text: The Ashikaga Shogunate was based in this city of Japan, which was known as Heian during an earlier period. It's not Tokyo, but the english translation for this city is "capital city."
question.clue: Henry Stimson, the US Secretary of War, is said to have honeymooned here, and famously lobbied to have this city taken off the list of bombing targets during the Second World War despite significant protests from the military.

swap.text: The LDP was founded during the reign of this emperor, who published numerous scientific papers about Hydrozoa. His reign included his delivery of the Jewel Voice Broadcast.
swap.clue: This ruler, who delivered the Jewel Voice Broadcast, later renounced his divinity in the Humanity Declaration.

question.leadin: Of the hundreds of exploding balloons sent by this group to the U.S., only one managed to cause any damage, landing in Oregon and killing several schoolchildren who checked it out.
question.text: Name this group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.
question.answerHtml: Unit 731 [or Nana-san-ichi Butai, or Manchu Detachment 731, or 731 Regiment, or Ishii Unit]
question.clue: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.

swap.leadin: Moderator note: do not reveal the alternate answer to the first bonus part. The man who negotiated this treaty gave the emperor an ultimatum from President Fillmore and then left the country for a year.
swap.text: Identify this 1854 treaty which opened up the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate in Japan to American trade.
swap.clue: Signed aboard the USS Powhatan, one provision of it mandated hospitality to shipwrecked sailors and their free travel within certain limits.

question.text: After moving his capital to Kamakura, Minamoto no Yoritomo took this title, making him the military ruler of Japan. The daimyos were feudal lords subservient to holders of this title, which was later taken by Tokugawa Ieyasu.
question.clue: A power vacuum created after the death of a holder of this title led to the Onin War, which initiated the Sengoku period.

swap.leadin: This man's favorite pastime was falconry.
swap.text: Name this victor at the Battle of Sekigahara, who signed the Christian Expulsion Edict in 1614. His forces successfully besieged Osaka to kill Toyotomi Hideyori.
swap.answerHtml: Tokugawa Ieyasu [or Matsudaira Takechiyo, either part, or Motonobu or Motoyasu]
swap.clue: After being designated Hideyori's regent, he defeated Ishida Mitsunari's Eastern Army at Sekigahara.

question.text: In the Kenmu restoration, Go-Daigo had usurped power from this shogunate. It was ruled by the Minamoto and Hojo families.
question.clue: During much of this period, political control rested with the shikken or regent, an office which was held hereditarily by the Hojo Family.

swap.text: The post-World War II Japanese constitution contained this article, which renounced the national right to war and use of force in international disputes. Despite this article, Japan maintains self-defense forces that serve as a de facto military.

question.leadin: The massive temple complex of Todai-ji was constructed during this period as the center of a system of provincial temples known as kokubun-ji.
question.text: Name this period of Japanese history in the 8th century that began with the establishment of Heijo-kyo as the capital. This period was followed by the Heian ("HAY-on") period.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.leadin: These laws brought about the development of estates called shoen.
swap.text: Name this set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.
swap.clue: The Asuka period ended with this set of reforms promulgated by the Kotoku Emperor which centralized power and introduced reorganization based on Tang Chinese lines.

question.leadin: This cultural phenomenon suppressed by the government's Bansha no goku program led to Hanaoka Seishu performing the first breast cancer surgery under general anesthesia.
question.text: Name this late Edo Period trend of translating and studying European texts, especially scientific ones, entering through Dejima island. It contrasts with a movement associated with Motoori ("moh-toh-OH-ree") Norinaga.
question.answerHtml: rangaku [or Dutch Learning; prompt on Western Learning] (Motoori was one of the leading lights of kokugaku or “National Learning,” i.e. Japanese classicism.)

swap.leadin: Kosaku Yamada wrote an opera titled for these vessels.
swap.text: Identify these European vessels that arrived annually at Nagasaki during the period of Japanese isolation.
swap.clue: Foreign boats that visited Japan during its periods of relative isolation were given this nickname. This nickname was also applied to Commodore Matthew Perry's ships that opened trade relations with Japan in the 1850s.

question.text: The foremost predecessor of the LDP was the Liberal Party, which was led by this towering figure of post-WWII Japanese politics. He served as Prime Minister five times between 1946 and 1954, and formulated a namesake Doctrine for Japan's postwar recovery.

swap.leadin: Frank Capra used this document as evidence in his propaganda film Why We Fight.
swap.text: Name this probably fictitious document which called for conquest of Manchuria and China as the path to Japanese dominance in East Asia.
swap.clue: James Cagney starred in a film based on a fictional scenario in which this document is smuggled to the United States, Blood on the Sun, and it is heavily featured in Frank Capra's Why We Fight.
